movement_profile.footwork: Rhythmic stepping and leaping matching the drum beats
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Mass group procession starting at Kochambalam temple, circumambulating the Vavar mosque, and moving 0.5 km to Valiyambalam Sastha temple
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Dynamic torso movement naturally moving with energetic group steps
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Upright stepping with occasional energetic hops/jumps
movement_profile.posture: Energetic, dynamic upright posture adapted for group processing and rhythmic stepping

signature_moves.description: Rhythmic stepping and leaping while chanting 'Ayyappa thinthakathom, Swamy thinthakathom' and brandishing wooden weapons.
signature_moves.name: Petta Thullal Step

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Do not execute without respecting sacred vows and ritual purity rules (vrata kalam).

music_profile.musical_form: Continuous ritual procession music driven by drum ensembles and response chanting
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Rhythmic accompaniment matched to the chant 'Ayyappa thinthakathom, Swamy thinthakathom'
music_profile.sound_description: A powerful, resonant outdoor ritual sound environment dominated by the thunderous percussion of Chenda melam and Pambamelam, melodic lines from the Nagaswaram, and the collective vocal shouting and chanting of thousands of pilgrims.
music_profile.vocal_style: Group chanting of mantras, hymns, and the refrain 'Ayyappa thinthakathom, Swamy thinthakathom'

basic_steps: Smear face and body with charcoal and colours as part of ritual preparation.
Hold a wooden arrow (sarakkol) or wooden mace in hand while supporting the shoulder bundle if a Kanni Ayyappa.
Step in a rhythmic, leaping group movement while chanting 'Ayyappa thinthakathom, Swamy thinthakathom'.
Process in rhythm from Kochambalam temple around the Vavar mosque and along the 0.5 km path to Valiyambalam Sastha temple.
teaching.formation: Group procession / free-form collective group movement.
teaching.level_notes: Ritual performance intended for spiritual devotees rather than formal dance stage instruction.
teaching.rhythm: Rhythmic driving beat marked by Chenda melam, Pambamelam, and vocal chants.
